tasks.short: Establish classroom rules and maintain order

steps.what: Establish and explain rules for behavior and classroom routines
Reinforce expectations and respond to behavior to maintain order

tasks.design: Keep rule explanation, reinforcement and classroom responses with the teacher. School policy in {DOCS} supports practice; no behaviour scoring, emotion inference or automated enforcement is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Children need consistent adult modelling and responses suited to the immediate situation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing school guidance already supports the retained human work.
tasks.still_hard: The same outward behaviour can arise from different needs or circumstances.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, set clear limits and respond proportionately to the child.
tasks.altitude: Classroom authority, relationship work and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Explaining and reinforcing classroom expectations retains its labour; the digest's lesson and record tools do not replace this interaction.

assumptions: Boundary is classroom rule setting and reinforcement; formal incident documentation and separate pupil support planning are outside the task.
No new structured behaviour flag, model classification or data capture is required.
Existing native policy access remains sufficient. No deployment or additional maintenance is introduced, justifying zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Classroom needs and school behaviour policy
research_questions: Which routines help children understand expectations without repeated disruption?

already_counted.description: Rule explanation and live classroom responses

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. Classroom explanation and response remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Encourage children to explore learning opportunities and persevere with challenging tasks

tasks.design: Keep encouragement and responsive support with the teacher during play and learning. Existing activity ideas in {DOCS} remain available; no automated motivational coach is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful encouragement depends on the child's effort, frustration and readiness for help.
tasks.enabler_now: No technology change removes the need for a trusted adult response.
tasks.still_hard: Too much help can remove the challenge while too little can discourage the child.
tasks.human_edge: Choose when to model, prompt, reassure or let the child try independently.
tasks.altitude: Encouragement and developmental support retain the same time and responsibility.

reach.task: Support a child who avoids challenging activities
reach.learn: Play-based scaffolding and appropriate support thresholds

evidence.claim: Live encouragement and responsive scaffolding retain all labour in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is encouraging exploration and perseverance during activity. Subject instruction and classroom discipline are assigned to other tasks and are not saved here.
No new structured motivation score or automated child assessment is introduced.
Existing native activity references suffice. No system or process is added, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Individual support needs and classroom context
research_questions: Which prompts support independent attempts rather than completing the task for the child?

incremental.description: No added system or workflow upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, zero gross and net saving. No adult encouragement or observation is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Instruct students individually and in groups, adapting methods to their responses

tasks.design: Keep responsive individual and group instruction with the teacher. Existing resources in {LMS} or {DOCS} may support the activity, without replacing live adaptation or introducing pupil profiling.
tasks.previous_blocker: The appropriate explanation or activity changes as children respond.
tasks.enabler_now: Prepared resources already support teaching but do not remove this live judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A group can contain several different needs at the same moment.
tasks.human_edge: Notice who needs a different demonstration, pace or form of participation.
tasks.altitude: Live instructional responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Support a group under the teacher's direction
reach.learn: Activity goals and when to seek teacher help

evidence.claim: The digest distinguishes lesson preparation tools from human instruction and adaptation; no direct-teaching saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is responsive delivery and adjustment to individual or group needs. Planned material production and basic-skill demonstrations are owned by their separate tasks; team roll-ups must allocate overlapping instruction once.
No new structured learner profile or automated teaching decision is required.
Use existing native resource access. No deployment or additional maintenance is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Class composition and division of teaching support duties
research_questions: Which observed responses call for a different instructional approach?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. Live adaptation remains fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach basic academic, personal and social skills

steps.what: Teach recognition, personal hygiene and social skills through demonstration and guided practice

tasks.design: Keep demonstrations and guided practice of colours, shapes, numbers, letters, hygiene and social skills with the teacher. Existing activity resources in {DOCS} support delivery without a new software step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Young children need concrete examples, adult modelling and feedback during practice.
tasks.enabler_now: No technical change removes those interactions within the chosen service.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising a symbol in one activity does not establish understanding in another.
tasks.human_edge: Connect simple concepts to the child's experience and model social and personal routines.
tasks.altitude: Basic-skill teaching duties and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Basic-skill demonstration and guided practice retain their labour; preparation-tool results do not establish direct teaching savings.

assumptions: Boundary is direct basic-skill demonstration and practice, excluding resource preparation. If a delivery episode also appears under task 6501, the roll-up assigns the episode here and only distinct adaptive effort there; no duplicated saving is claimed.
No machine depends on a structured child-performance or hygiene-completion flag.
Existing native resources remain sufficient. No new system or ongoing process is added, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Current activity sequence and learner needs
research_questions: Can children apply the demonstrated skill in another familiar context?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. No guided practice or adult modelling is removed.

reach: Coordinate appropriate support with early years specialists
